Task: List five surprising facts about the Roman Empire.

• Romans used concrete that could set and harden underwater—a recipe so durable that many harbor structures built 2,000 years ago are still intact.  
• For more than two centuries (27 BCE–180 CE) the empire enjoyed the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace so extensive that frontier soldiers were sometimes paid to farm instead of fight.  
• Roman apartment blocks (insulae) in cities like Rome and Ostia routinely rose 5–7 stories high, rivaling modern mid-rise buildings in both height and population density.  
• Emperor Elagabalus (reigned 218–222 CE) reportedly installed a revolving dining room ceiling that could shower guests with petals and perfume—an ancient example of theatrical engineering.  
• Lead-pipe plumbing was widespread, yet analysis of Roman skeletons shows no epidemic lead poisoning; the high calcium content of their water formed mineral layers that insulated drinkers from the metal.
